elements.scope_reason: 'Serious drug reaction likely' with a rash criterion and a 3-month time window.
elements.problem: Diffuse rash -> 'Generalized rash' (SNOMED lists 'diffuse rash' as its synonym). 'Within 3 months of starting a new medication' -> onset of 'New medication commenced' <= time_ago 3 months, which under the house convention (briefing: '(< (onset X) (time_ago 3 days))' means within the last 3 days) reads as 'started within the last 3 months'. Strictly the page bounds the rash's appearance relative to the medication start, not the medication start relative to today; the encoding is the closest the language offers and the difference only matters for a rash that appeared long after a medication started more than 3 months ago (which the encoding correctly excludes) or a rash that appeared promptly after a medication started 2 months ago (correctly included). Rule type probable; Urgent priority references the active condition. Diagnosis concept 'Adverse reaction caused by drug' is the right breadth: 'Eruption caused by drug' exists but would not cover shock, jaundice or diarrhoea.

parts_missing: Footnote 2: no probable Shock rule. Of its five criteria only SBP < 80 appears (as a criterion of the drug reaction rule); pulse >= 100, respiratory rate > 30, decreased level of consciousness and weakness are not encoded anywhere, so a patient with a diffuse rash on a new medication who has tachycardia, RR > 30 or weakness but a recorded SBP of 85 does not meet the 'Shock' arm unless a clinician records 'Shock' by hand. SNOMED has 'Decreased level of consciousness' (finding), 'Muscle weakness' (finding) and 'Tachycardia' (finding); pulse and respiratory rate are routine measurements.

Footnote 1: 'within the past few hours' is not applied to the drug/food exposure or insect bite/sting findings in the anaphylaxis rule. The language can bound onset of a finding; 'few hours' is vague, so this is minor.

summary: The red box is fully and correctly encoded: every criterion of the anaphylaxis, meningococcal and serious drug reaction bullets is present with the right concept, threshold, direction and rule type, all 57 SNOMED concepts resolve, and every check_for item is consumed by a rule. The one substantive miss is footnote 2's definition of shock (SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, RR > 30, decreased consciousness, weakness: 'shock likely'), which has no probable rule, so the drug reaction rule's Shock arm only fires on SBP < 80 or a hand-recorded diagnosis. The mpox 'consider' sentence is correctly a possible rule; the flowchart boxes and the HIV-test line are routing/management and out of scope.
